I'm fully conscious but just feel disconnected, like I'm trapped in slow motion staring at my hands while knowing I need to hurry, even though my crew also points out how off I'm acting.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other episodes or situations outside of work where you felt this sense of disconnection or being 'on a different channel', such as during everyday activities or when under no particular stress?\n\nPatient: No, that freezing feeling only really happens during those high-pressure calls at work. Outside of work, I don't freeze up like that, but I just feel completely flat, empty, and exhausted. I mostly just sit alone in my apartment now and don't really have the energy to see my friends or do anything.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about feeling 'flat, empty, and exhausted' outside of work, is this something that started after these work incidents or was it present before?\n\nPatient: This flat feeling really started after we responded to a terrible multi-car pileup on I-95 about ten months ago. Before that, I was always active with running, fishing, and playing basketball, but since then, I just sit in my apartment and can't even bring myself to reply to my friends' texts. I just feel completely empty and tired inside now.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you used to enjoy activities like running, fishing, and basketball, but now you can't bring yourself to do them. Do you still find any pleasure or interest in these activities, or have they become completely unenjoyable for you?\n\nPatient: They aren't enjoyable at all anymore, and I don't feel any interest in them. I just feel completely flat and tired inside, to the point where I don't even care enough to get off the couch or text my friends back. I remember really loving those things before, but now it just feels like nothing.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel guilty about what happened during the multi-car pileup on I-95, or is there something specific about that incident that you replay in your mind and wish you had handled differently?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel guilty or have specific regrets about my actions that day. It's more that the sheer chaos and emotional intensity of the whole scene just deeply shook me, and I haven't been able to get past it.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling empty and tired, and losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but do you still have the ability to feel happy or experience any moments of pleasure, even if it's just briefly?\n\nPatient: No, I really don't feel any happiness or pleasure anymore, not even briefly. Even when I think about things I used to love like fishing or basketball, I just don't feel that spark or care anymore. It all just feels completely flat and empty inside.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have any flashbacks or nightmares related to the multi-car pileup incident, or if you try to avoid thinking or talking about it?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have flashbacks or nightmares about the pileup, and I don't try to avoid thinking about it. While it was a chaotic and stressful event, I don't re-experience it in those ways. My main struggles are just feeling so out of sync and overwhelmed on calls, like I described.\n\nDoctor: You've described feeling disconnected and 'on a different channel' during high-stress calls, but also feeling flat and empty outside of work. Can you tell me if these feelings of being disconnected and empty are constant, or if they vary in intensity over time?\n\nPatient: The feeling of being on a different channel and disconnected is most intense and noticeable during emergency calls when I'm expected to move fast. In contrast, the flat, tired, and empty feeling outside of work is more of a constant, heavy state that just lingers whenever I'm at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the feeling of being 'flat, empty, and exhausted' outside of work is more related to a lack of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or if it's a feeling of emotional numbing, where you just can't feel any emotions at all, even if you wanted to?\n\nPatient: It really feels like a mix of both, but the biggest thing is just this complete lack of energy and drive. I feel so flat and tired inside that I don't even care enough to get off the couch or answer texts from my buddies, even though I remember enjoying fishing and basketball so much before. It's just a total loss of motivation and interest.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions, such as sadness, anger, or happiness, when something significant happens, or is it all just feeling flat and empty to you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really feel a full range of emotions anymore; it's just a constant flat and tired feeling inside. Even when my brother asks me to go fishing or my buddies text me to play basketball, I just feel empty and don't care enough to answer or get off the couch.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's anything that triggers or worsens the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or if it's solely related to the high-stress environment itself?\n\nPatient: It is mostly triggered by those highly chaotic moments on scene, especially when things are moving fast and people are shouting directions at me to hurry. This pattern of freezing and going into slow motion really took hold after that big pileup on I-95, and now any fast-paced emergency call seems to bring it on.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any significant emotional responses you've had recently, such as intense fear, anxiety, or irritability, especially in relation to your work or the incident on I-95?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel intense fear or anger about the I-95 crash anymore; instead, I just feel completely flat and tired inside with no energy to care about anything. However, I have been feeling really stressed and unsettled lately because I'm convinced dispatch and the hospital staff are putting hidden codes in the radio traffic and chart notes to track my mistakes and get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these hidden codes you believe are being used by dispatch and the hospital staff, and how you think they're related to your work performance or the possibility of getting fired?\n\nPatient: It really feels like dispatch and some of the hospital staff are slipping little codes into the radio traffic and chart notes specifically about me to track how I mess up on calls. They are building a case to get me fired, and even though my supervisor swears it's all just routine paperwork, it feels incredibly real and deliberate to me. It's been happening for the last couple of months, and it's making me feel constantly on edge.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, besides the hidden codes, for why dispatch and hospital staff might be discussing your performance or making notes about your work, or do you firmly believe it's all part of a plot against you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor keeps telling me it's just routine paperwork, but I firmly believe there is more to it than that. The codes in the radio traffic and the chart notes are just too specific and coordinated to be a coincidence. I truly believe they are using them to build a case to get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would change your mind about the existence of these hidden codes, or do you believe they are absolutely real regardless of what others say or any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor swears it is just routine paperwork, the feeling that they are tracking me and sending these hidden messages feels incredibly real and hard to ignore. Because of how clear it is to me, it's really difficult to imagine any evidence that would completely change my mind right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the hidden codes affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief is related to your feelings of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls?\n\nPatient: The belief about the codes makes me incredibly anxious and paranoid, which contributes to why I withdraw from my friends and stay isolated in my apartment. It's definitely connected to being 'on a different channel' because on scene, I get so distracted and overwhelmed trying to figure out if people are watching me or sending coded messages that my brain freezes. That distraction is what makes me feel completely disconnected from the fast-paced environment around me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any way to prove or disprove the existence of these hidden codes, such as asking someone you trust to review the radio traffic and chart notes with you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor already looked at the paperwork and insisted it's just routine, so I don't think having someone else review it would help. Besides, these codes are meant specifically for me, so I doubt anyone else would even be able to see or understand them. I'm just worried they would dismiss my concerns and think I'm losing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief in the hidden codes is related to the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or are these two separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel connected to me. The codes in the radio traffic and notes seem to be tracking the exact mistakes I make on calls, which is when my body goes on that different channel and I freeze up. It's like they are documenting every time I get stuck in slow motion and can't keep up."

This pattern of freezing and going into slow motion really took hold after that big pileup on I-95, and now any fast-paced emergency call seems to bring it on.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any significant emotional responses you've had recently, such as intense fear, anxiety, or irritability, especially in relation to your work or the incident on I-95?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel intense fear or anger about the I-95 crash anymore; instead, I just feel completely flat and tired inside with no energy to care about anything. However, I have been feeling really stressed and unsettled lately because I'm convinced dispatch and the hospital staff are putting hidden codes in the radio traffic and chart notes to track my mistakes and get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these hidden codes you believe are being used by dispatch and the hospital staff, and how you think they're related to your work performance or the possibility of getting fired?\n\nPatient: It really feels like dispatch and some of the hospital staff are slipping little codes into the radio traffic and chart notes specifically about me to track how I mess up on calls. Because of how clear it is to me, it's really difficult to imagine any evidence that would completely change my mind right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the hidden codes affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief is related to your feelings of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls?\n\nPatient: The belief about the codes makes me incredibly anxious and paranoid, which contributes to why I withdraw from my friends and stay isolated in my apartment. My crew says I'm acting really off, and my supervisor ended up pulling me from the field to get this evaluation before I can go back to work.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about what you mean by 'moving wrong' and 'doing the wrong things'? Do you feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself, or like things around you aren't real?\n\nPatient: It's not really like I'm outside my body or that things aren't real, but more like my body is suddenly on a completely different channel. During high-stress calls, I'll just freeze and stare at my hands while people are shouting instructions, or find myself doing something weirdly slow and meticulous like re-rolling bandages while everyone else is moving fast.\n\nDoctor: Do you remember everything that happens during these episodes, or are there parts that you don't recall until later, like your crew tells you about them?\n\nPatient: I actually remember everything quite clearly; I don't black out or forget. I'm fully conscious but just feel disconnected, like I'm trapped in slow motion staring at my hands while knowing I need to hurry, even though my crew also points out how off I'm acting.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other episodes or situations outside of work where you felt this sense of disconnection or being 'on a different channel', such as during everyday activities or when under no particular stress?\n\nPatient: No, that freezing feeling only really happens during those high-pressure calls at work. Outside of work, I don't freeze up like that, but I just feel completely flat, empty, and exhausted. I mostly just sit alone in my apartment now and don't really have the energy to see my friends or do anything.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about feeling 'flat, empty, and exhausted' outside of work, is this something that started after these work incidents or was it present before?\n\nPatient: This flat feeling really started after we responded to a terrible multi-car pileup on I-95 about ten months ago. Before that, I was always active with running, fishing, and playing basketball, but since then, I just sit in my apartment and can't even bring myself to reply to my friends' texts. I just feel completely empty and tired inside now.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you used to enjoy activities like running, fishing, and basketball, but now you can't bring yourself to do them. Do you still find any pleasure or interest in these activities, or have they become completely unenjoyable for you?\n\nPatient: They aren't enjoyable at all anymore, and I don't feel any interest in them. I just feel completely flat and tired inside, to the point where I don't even care enough to get off the couch or text my friends back. I remember really loving those things before, but now it just feels like nothing.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel guilty about what happened during the multi-car pileup on I-95, or is there something specific about that incident that you replay in your mind and wish you had handled differently?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel guilty or have specific regrets about my actions that day. It's more that the sheer chaos and emotional intensity of the whole scene just deeply shook me, and I haven't been able to get past it.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling empty and tired, and losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but do you still have the ability to feel happy or experience any moments of pleasure, even if it's just briefly?\n\nPatient: No, I really don't feel any happiness or pleasure anymore, not even briefly. Even when I think about things I used to love like fishing or basketball, I just don't feel that spark or care anymore. It all just feels completely flat and empty inside.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have any flashbacks or nightmares related to the multi-car pileup incident, or if you try to avoid thinking or talking about it?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have flashbacks or nightmares about the pileup, and I don't try to avoid thinking about it. While it was a chaotic and stressful event, I don't re-experience it in those ways. My main struggles are just feeling so out of sync and overwhelmed on calls, like I described.\n\nDoctor: You've described feeling disconnected and 'on a different channel' during high-stress calls, but also feeling flat and empty outside of work. Can you tell me if these feelings of being disconnected and empty are constant, or if they vary in intensity over time?\n\nPatient: The feeling of being on a different channel and disconnected is most intense and noticeable during emergency calls when I'm expected to move fast. In contrast, the flat, tired, and empty feeling outside of work is more of a constant, heavy state that just lingers whenever I'm at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the feeling of being 'flat, empty, and exhausted' outside of work is more related to a lack of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or if it's a feeling of emotional numbing, where you just can't feel any emotions at all, even if you wanted to?\n\nPatient: It really feels like a mix of both, but the biggest thing is just this complete lack of energy and drive. I feel so flat and tired inside that I don't even care enough to get off the couch or answer texts from my buddies, even though I remember enjoying fishing and basketball so much before. It's just a total loss of motivation and interest.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions, such as sadness, anger, or happiness, when something significant happens, or is it all just feeling flat and empty to you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really feel a full range of emotions anymore; it's just a constant flat and tired feeling inside. Even when my brother asks me to go fishing or my buddies text me to play basketball, I just feel empty and don't care enough to answer or get off the couch.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's anything that triggers or worsens the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or if it's solely related to the high-stress environment itself?\n\nPatient: It is mostly triggered by those highly chaotic moments on scene, especially when things are moving fast and people are shouting directions at me to hurry. This pattern of freezing and going into slow motion really took hold after that big pileup on I-95, and now any fast-paced emergency call seems to bring it on.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any significant emotional responses you've had recently, such as intense fear, anxiety, or irritability, especially in relation to your work or the incident on I-95?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel intense fear or anger about the I-95 crash anymore; instead, I just feel completely flat and tired inside with no energy to care about anything. However, I have been feeling really stressed and unsettled lately because I'm convinced dispatch and the hospital staff are putting hidden codes in the radio traffic and chart notes to track my mistakes and get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these hidden codes you believe are being used by dispatch and the hospital staff, and how you think they're related to your work performance or the possibility of getting fired?\n\nPatient: It really feels like dispatch and some of the hospital staff are slipping little codes into the radio traffic and chart notes specifically about me to track how I mess up on calls. They are building a case to get me fired, and even though my supervisor swears it's all just routine paperwork, it feels incredibly real and deliberate to me. It's been happening for the last couple of months, and it's making me feel constantly on edge.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, besides the hidden codes, for why dispatch and hospital staff might be discussing your performance or making notes about your work, or do you firmly believe it's all part of a plot against you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor keeps telling me it's just routine paperwork, but I firmly believe there is more to it than that. The codes in the radio traffic and the chart notes are just too specific and coordinated to be a coincidence. I truly believe they are using them to build a case to get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would change your mind about the existence of these hidden codes, or do you believe they are absolutely real regardless of what others say or any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor swears it is just routine paperwork, the feeling that they are tracking me and sending these hidden messages feels incredibly real and hard to ignore. Because of how clear it is to me, it's really difficult to imagine any evidence that would completely change my mind right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the hidden codes affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief is related to your feelings of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls?\n\nPatient: The belief about the codes makes me incredibly anxious and paranoid, which contributes to why I withdraw from my friends and stay isolated in my apartment. It's definitely connected to being 'on a different channel' because on scene, I get so distracted and overwhelmed trying to figure out if people are watching me or sending coded messages that my brain freezes. That distraction is what makes me feel completely disconnected from the fast-paced environment around me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any way to prove or disprove the existence of these hidden codes, such as asking someone you trust to review the radio traffic and chart notes with you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor already looked at the paperwork and insisted it's just routine, so I don't think having someone else review it would help. Besides, these codes are meant specifically for me, so I doubt anyone else would even be able to see or understand them. I'm just worried they would dismiss my concerns and think I'm losing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief in the hidden codes is related to the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or are these two separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel connected to me. The codes in the radio traffic and notes seem to be tracking the exact mistakes I make on calls, which is when my body goes on that different channel and I freeze up. It's like they are documenting every time I get stuck in slow motion and can't keep up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls and the belief that there are hidden codes being used against you, and do you think one causes the other?\n\nPatient: Being \"on a different channel\" is a physical and mental disconnect where my body freezes up and I can't keep up with the emergency, while the hidden codes are a distressing belief that people are actively plotting to get me fired. They feel different—one is about my body not cooperating and the other is about people targeting me—but they are connected because my freezing mistakes on scene give them more reason to watch and code my performance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in the hidden codes and your feeling of being 'on a different channel' could be related to a single underlying issue, rather than two separate problems?\n\nPatient: I hadn't really thought of them as the same thing before, but both of these experiences started happening around the same period as I began to unravel. The codes still feel completely real and stressful to me, but both situations make me feel totally disconnected from everyone and like my mind and body just aren't working the way they used to.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where you felt like you were in a dream or detached from reality outside of the emergency calls, or if these feelings of disconnection are strictly related to the high-stress situations at work?\n\nPatient: That physical feeling of being on a different channel and freezing up only happens during those high-pressure emergency calls. Outside of work, I don't really experience that kind of disconnection; instead, I just feel completely flat, tired, and isolated. I mostly just want to stay on my couch all day and avoid everyone.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation where your belief in the hidden codes might be proven wrong, and if so, how would you cope with that realization?"

Even when my brother asks me to go fishing or my buddies text me to play basketball, I just feel empty and don't care enough to answer or get off the couch.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's anything that triggers or worsens the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or if it's solely related to the high-stress environment itself?\n\nPatient: It is mostly triggered by those highly chaotic moments on scene, especially when things are moving fast and people are shouting directions at me to hurry. This pattern of freezing and going into slow motion really took hold after that big pileup on I-95, and now any fast-paced emergency call seems to bring it on.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any significant emotional responses you've had recently, such as intense fear, anxiety, or irritability, especially in relation to your work or the incident on I-95?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel intense fear or anger about the I-95 crash anymore; instead, I just feel completely flat and tired inside with no energy to care about anything. However, I have been feeling really stressed and unsettled lately because I'm convinced dispatch and the hospital staff are putting hidden codes in the radio traffic and chart notes to track my mistakes and get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these hidden codes you believe are being used by dispatch and the hospital staff, and how you think they're related to your work performance or the possibility of getting fired?\n\nPatient: It really feels like dispatch and some of the hospital staff are slipping little codes into the radio traffic and chart notes specifically about me to track how I mess up on calls. They are building a case to get me fired, and even though my supervisor swears it's all just routine paperwork, it feels incredibly real and deliberate to me. It's been happening for the last couple of months, and it's making me feel constantly on edge.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, besides the hidden codes, for why dispatch and hospital staff might be discussing your performance or making notes about your work, or do you firmly believe it's all part of a plot against you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor keeps telling me it's just routine paperwork, but I firmly believe there is more to it than that. The codes in the radio traffic and the chart notes are just too specific and coordinated to be a coincidence. I truly believe they are using them to build a case to get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would change your mind about the existence of these hidden codes, or do you believe they are absolutely real regardless of what others say or any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor swears it is just routine paperwork, the feeling that they are tracking me and sending these hidden messages feels incredibly real and hard to ignore. Because of how clear it is to me, it's really difficult to imagine any evidence that would completely change my mind right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the hidden codes affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief is related to your feelings of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls?\n\nPatient: The belief about the codes makes me incredibly anxious and paranoid, which contributes to why I withdraw from my friends and stay isolated in my apartment. The codes still feel completely real and stressful to me, but both situations make me feel totally disconnected from everyone and like my mind and body just aren't working the way they used to.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where you felt like you were in a dream or detached from reality outside of the emergency calls, or if these feelings of disconnection are strictly related to the high-stress situations at work?\n\nPatient: That physical feeling of being on a different channel and freezing up only happens during those high-pressure emergency calls. I mostly just want to stay on my couch all day and avoid everyone.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation where your belief in the hidden codes might be proven wrong, and if so, how would you cope with that realization?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about what would happen if it was proven wrong, because it feels so incredibly real to me right now. Because of how clear it is to me, it's really difficult to imagine any evidence that would completely change my mind right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the hidden codes affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief is related to your feelings of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls?\n\nPatient: The belief about the codes makes me incredibly anxious and paranoid, which contributes to why I withdraw from my friends and stay isolated in my apartment. It's definitely connected to being 'on a different channel' because on scene, I get so distracted and overwhelmed trying to figure out if people are watching me or sending coded messages that my brain freezes. That distraction is what makes me feel completely disconnected from the fast-paced environment around me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any way to prove or disprove the existence of these hidden codes, such as asking someone you trust to review the radio traffic and chart notes with you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor already looked at the paperwork and insisted it's just routine, so I don't think having someone else review it would help. Besides, these codes are meant specifically for me, so I doubt anyone else would even be able to see or understand them. I'm just worried they would dismiss my concerns and think I'm losing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief in the hidden codes is related to the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or are these two separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel connected to me. It's like they are documenting every time I get stuck in slow motion and can't keep up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls and the belief that there are hidden codes being used against you, and do you think one causes the other?\n\nPatient: Being \"on a different channel\" is a physical and mental disconnect where my body freezes up and I can't keep up with the emergency, while the hidden codes are a distressing belief that people are actively plotting to get me fired. They feel different—one is about my body not cooperating and the other is about people targeting me—but they are connected because my freezing mistakes on scene give them more reason to watch and code my performance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in the hidden codes and your feeling of being 'on a different channel' could be related to a single underlying issue, rather than two separate problems?\n\nPatient: I hadn't really thought of them as the same thing before, but both of these experiences started happening around the same period as I began to unravel. The codes still feel completely real and stressful to me, but both situations make me feel totally disconnected from everyone and like my mind and body just aren't working the way they used to.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where you felt like you were in a dream or detached from reality outside of the emergency calls, or if these feelings of disconnection are strictly related to the high-stress situations at work?\n\nPatient: That physical feeling of being on a different channel and freezing up only happens during those high-pressure emergency calls. I mostly just sit alone in my apartment now and don't really have the energy to see my friends or do anything.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about feeling 'flat, empty, and exhausted' outside of work, is this something that started after these work incidents or was it present before?\n\nPatient: This flat feeling really started after we responded to a terrible multi-car pileup on I-95 about ten months ago. Before that, I was always active with running, fishing, and playing basketball, but since then, I just sit in my apartment and can't even bring myself to reply to my friends' texts. I just feel completely empty and tired inside now.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you used to enjoy activities like running, fishing, and basketball, but now you can't bring yourself to do them. Do you still find any pleasure or interest in these activities, or have they become completely unenjoyable for you?\n\nPatient: They aren't enjoyable at all anymore, and I don't feel any interest in them. I just feel completely flat and tired inside, to the point where I don't even care enough to get off the couch or text my friends back. I remember really loving those things before, but now it just feels like nothing.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel guilty about what happened during the multi-car pileup on I-95, or is there something specific about that incident that you replay in your mind and wish you had handled differently?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel guilty or have specific regrets about my actions that day. It's more that the sheer chaos and emotional intensity of the whole scene just deeply shook me, and I haven't been able to get past it.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling empty and tired, and losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but do you still have the ability to feel happy or experience any moments of pleasure, even if it's just briefly?\n\nPatient: No, I really don't feel any happiness or pleasure anymore, not even briefly. Even when I think about things I used to love like fishing or basketball, I just don't feel that spark or care anymore. It all just feels completely flat and empty inside.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have any flashbacks or nightmares related to the multi-car pileup incident, or if you try to avoid thinking or talking about it?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have flashbacks or nightmares about the pileup, and I don't try to avoid thinking about it. While it was a chaotic and stressful event, I don't re-experience it in those ways. My main struggles are just feeling so out of sync and overwhelmed on calls, like I described.\n\nDoctor: You've described feeling disconnected and 'on a different channel' during high-stress calls, but also feeling flat and empty outside of work. Can you tell me if these feelings of being disconnected and empty are constant, or if they vary in intensity over time?\n\nPatient: The feeling of being on a different channel and disconnected is most intense and noticeable during emergency calls when I'm expected to move fast. In contrast, the flat, tired, and empty feeling outside of work is more of a constant, heavy state that just lingers whenever I'm at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the feeling of being 'flat, empty, and exhausted' outside of work is more related to a lack of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or if it's a feeling of emotional numbing, where you just can't feel any emotions at all, even if you wanted to?\n\nPatient: It really feels like a mix of both, but the biggest thing is just this complete lack of energy and drive. I feel so flat and tired inside that I don't even care enough to get off the couch or answer texts from my buddies, even though I remember enjoying fishing and basketball so much before. It's just a total loss of motivation and interest.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions, such as sadness, anger, or happiness, when something significant happens, or is it all just feeling flat and empty to you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really feel a full range of emotions anymore; it's just a constant flat and tired feeling inside. Even when my brother asks me to go fishing or my buddies text me to play basketball, I just feel empty and don't care enough to answer or get off the couch.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there's anything that triggers or worsens the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or if it's solely related to the high-stress environment itself?\n\nPatient: It is mostly triggered by those highly chaotic moments on scene, especially when things are moving fast and people are shouting directions at me to hurry. This pattern of freezing and going into slow motion really took hold after that big pileup on I-95, and now any fast-paced emergency call seems to bring it on.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any significant emotional responses you've had recently, such as intense fear, anxiety, or irritability, especially in relation to your work or the incident on I-95?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel intense fear or anger about the I-95 crash anymore; instead, I just feel completely flat and tired inside with no energy to care about anything. However, I have been feeling really stressed and unsettled lately because I'm convinced dispatch and the hospital staff are putting hidden codes in the radio traffic and chart notes to track my mistakes and get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these hidden codes you believe are being used by dispatch and the hospital staff, and how you think they're related to your work performance or the possibility of getting fired?\n\nPatient: It really feels like dispatch and some of the hospital staff are slipping little codes into the radio traffic and chart notes specifically about me to track how I mess up on calls. They are building a case to get me fired, and even though my supervisor swears it's all just routine paperwork, it feels incredibly real and deliberate to me. It's been happening for the last couple of months, and it's making me feel constantly on edge.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any other explanation, besides the hidden codes, for why dispatch and hospital staff might be discussing your performance or making notes about your work, or do you firmly believe it's all part of a plot against you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor keeps telling me it's just routine paperwork, but I firmly believe there is more to it than that. The codes in the radio traffic and the chart notes are just too specific and coordinated to be a coincidence. I truly believe they are using them to build a case to get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would change your mind about the existence of these hidden codes, or do you believe they are absolutely real regardless of what others say or any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor swears it is just routine paperwork, the feeling that they are tracking me and sending these hidden messages feels incredibly real and hard to ignore. Because of how clear it is to me, it's really difficult to imagine any evidence that would completely change my mind right now.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the hidden codes affects your daily life and interactions with others, and do you think this belief is related to your feelings of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls?\n\nPatient: The belief about the codes makes me incredibly anxious and paranoid, which contributes to why I withdraw from my friends and stay isolated in my apartment. It's definitely connected to being 'on a different channel' because on scene, I get so distracted and overwhelmed trying to figure out if people are watching me or sending coded messages that my brain freezes. That distraction is what makes me feel completely disconnected from the fast-paced environment around me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any way to prove or disprove the existence of these hidden codes, such as asking someone you trust to review the radio traffic and chart notes with you?\n\nPatient: My supervisor already looked at the paperwork and insisted it's just routine, so I don't think having someone else review it would help. Besides, these codes are meant specifically for me, so I doubt anyone else would even be able to see or understand them. I'm just worried they would dismiss my concerns and think I'm losing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief in the hidden codes is related to the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls, or are these two separate issues for you?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel connected to me. The codes in the radio traffic and notes seem to be tracking the exact mistakes I make on calls, which is when my body goes on that different channel and I freeze up. It's like they are documenting every time I get stuck in slow motion and can't keep up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the feeling of being 'on a different channel' during emergency calls and the belief that there are hidden codes being used against you, and do you think one causes the other?\n\nPatient: Being \"on a different channel\" is a physical and mental disconnect where my body freezes up and I can't keep up with the emergency, while the hidden codes are a distressing belief that people are actively plotting to get me fired. They feel different—one is about my body not cooperating and the other is about people targeting me—but they are connected because my freezing mistakes on scene give them more reason to watch and code my performance.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your belief in the hidden codes and your feeling of being 'on a different channel' could be related to a single underlying issue, rather than two separate problems?\n\nPatient: I hadn't really thought of them as the same thing before, but both of these experiences started happening around the same period as I began to unravel. The codes still feel completely real and stressful to me, but both situations make me feel totally disconnected from everyone and like my mind and body just aren't working the way they used to.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any experiences where you felt like you were in a dream or detached from reality outside of the emergency calls, or if these feelings of disconnection are strictly related to the high-stress situations at work?\n\nPatient: That physical feeling of being on a different channel and freezing up only happens during those high-pressure emergency calls. Outside of work, I don't really experience that kind of disconnection; instead, I just feel completely flat, tired, and isolated. I mostly just want to stay on my couch all day and avoid everyone.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation where your belief in the hidden codes might be proven wrong, and if so, how would you cope with that realization?\n\nPatient: I haven't really thought about what would happen if it was proven wrong, because it feels so incredibly real to me right now. It is really hard to imagine that it's not actually happening when I see the codes so clearly.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief in the hidden codes is something that you can control or change, or do you feel like it's something that's being forced upon you by others?\n\nPatient: I don't feel like I can easily control or change it, because the codes feel completely real and persistent to me. It's not that anyone is forcing the belief on me, but seeing them constantly is just so distressing and confusing. I really wish I could just shut it off, but I can't.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation where you saw one of these hidden codes, and how it made you feel, to help me understand what's going on?\n\nPatient: Just last week, right after I froze on a call, dispatch used a specific, unusual phrase over the radio, and later I saw a weirdly formatted timestamp in the chart notes that felt like a direct reference to my delay. It made me feel incredibly anxious and targeted, like they were actively documenting my failure. Even though my supervisor insists it's just routine paperwork, I am certain there is a hidden meaning behind it to build a case to get me fired.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would make you question the reality of the hidden codes, or do you believe they are absolutely real regardless of what others say or any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: I understand why you're asking, but it is really hard for me to doubt what I'm seeing. Even though my supervisor swears it is just routine paperwork and others might not see it, the feeling that dispatch and the hospital are tracking me to get me fired feels incredibly real and convincing. Right now, I just can't imagine any evidence that would prove it otherwise.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's any possibility that your belief in the hidden codes is not based on real events, but rather on your own fears or anxieties about your work performance?\n\nPatient: I am definitely very anxious and stressed about my performance on calls lately, and I've tried telling myself it's just my nerves playing tricks on me. But even with my supervisor insisting it's just routine paperwork, the codes feel too deliberate and specific to me to be just a coincidence or my imagination. It really feels like they are actively tracking my mistakes to build a case against me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever considered that your belief in the hidden codes might be a product of your own mind, rather than an actual plot against you, and how that would change your understanding of what's happening?\n\nPatient: It's really frightening to think my own mind could be making this up, but with all the stress since that I-95 crash, I suppose it's possible my brain is just struggling to process things. Even though the codes feel incredibly real and scary, the thought that my head is playing tricks on me is overwhelming. Either way, carrying this constant worry and trying to figure it out is just exhausting.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the hidden codes and your feeling of being 'on a different channel' are related to each other, or are they two completely separate things happening to you?"
